title: Back-of-the-mouth pairs: ق/ك · غ/خ

bigIdea.text: Two pairs sit at the back of the mouth. ق and ك are neighbours on the back of the tongue: ق deeper and heavy, ك a little forward and light. غ and خ share one place near the top of the throat: غ buzzes with voice, خ is only breath.

proper.text: Places: ق is the back of the tongue opposite the root of the uvula; ك is the back of the tongue with the roof of the mouth above it. Both are called 'uvula letters' (lahawiyyatan). غ and خ both come from the part of the throat nearest the mouth.

ق vs ك in sifat: both are strong (shiddah). ق holds the breath back (jahr), is raised (isti'la) and bounces with a sukun (qalqalah). ك is whispered (hams: the breath flows with it) and lowered (istifal).

provenance.title: صفة حرف (العربية) (Sifat of Arabic letters) — Arabic Wikipedia

proper.text: غ vs خ in sifat: both are raised (isti'la) and soft (rakhawa). The difference is the breath: غ holds it back (jahr); خ lets it flow (hams).

provenance.title: صفة حرف (العربية) (Sifat of Arabic letters) — Arabic Wikipedia

proper.text: Heavy or light: ق, غ and خ are heavy; ك is light. So ق/ك is a heavy/light pair, while غ and خ are both heavy.

Common mistakes. English speakers: ق said as ك, and غ or خ said as 'g' or 'k'. Persian readers: ق said like غ — ق must stop, غ must flow. Fix ق first (press the very back of the tongue, stop, release), then let غ flow from just behind it.

memoryHook.text: Qaf deep and heavy, kaf forward and light; ghayn buzzes, kha breathes.

extras.text: Linguists describe Arabic ك (like ت) as aspirated — said with a puff of air — and ق (like ط) as unaspirated.

note.text: Starts with خ and ends with ق.

tip.text: ق: the very back of the tongue presses near the uvula; heavy, no puff, and a bounce when it has a sukun. ك: a little further forward; light, with a small puff of breath.
Same place. Say خ (only breath, as in 'loch'), then add voice without moving anything: that is غ. Keep both heavy.

remnote: ق vs ك == ق: deepest back of the tongue, heavy, no puff, bounces with sukun; ك: a little forward, light, a little breath
غ vs خ == Same place near the top of the throat, both heavy; غ holds the breath (voice), خ lets it flow
Persian fix for ق and غ == ق stops; غ flows
